correctness.rationale: The physical update gives an exact lifted min-plus formula. The surplus n-(v+1)m is nonnegative, confining each car’s global minimum to m terms; a strict new minimum at the last term exactly characterizes T=m-1. Two disjoint negative arcs rule out multiple last-delayed cars. Reversing the m-1 active gaps gives the exact v-forest prefix condition, and the omitted gap is automatically admissible. Lagrange inversion proves the all-m,n,v formula. Direct binary and gap simulations plus an independent forest-coefficient program agree for 8 physical configurations families, 70 finite gap cases and 30 algebraic cases. Finite checks support, but do not replace, the all-parameter proof.

originality.rationale: The exact sharp relaxation time, its all-speed-v>=2 indexed multiplicity, ordered v-forest representation and fixed-surplus critical-window probability are not supplied by the examined primary traffic sources. The published speed-one Catalan result is an exact subfamily outside the claimed speed range; speed-one alone does not imply the v-ary forest result. A 1997 finite-convergence note and original 1996 paper were not fully accessible, creating a specific residual historical-priority risk. This is an evidence-bounded originality judgement, not a proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: The original 1996 model paper and the 1997 Wang–Wang–Hui finite-convergence note could not be inspected completely; unexamined text might state a stronger finite-size theorem.
Unindexed queueing/traffic literature might give an equivalent generalized ballot enumeration of the same *dynamical* event; the classical Raney combinatorial identity itself is not claimed novel.
The 1998 Physical Review E paper on statistical mechanical Fukui–Ishibashi flow was only available as an abstract, so more detailed related assertions in its full text remain unverified.

value.rationale: The natural finite-size relaxation clock for a canonical high-speed traffic automaton has a sharp all-parameter extremal population, and the exact event has positive fixed-surplus limiting probability rather than becoming exponentially rare. The v-component full-ary forest classification explains a qualitative, speed-dependent extension of the known Catalan v=1 structure, while supplying a reusable finite-size diagnostic for high-speed traffic flow. The object and invariant arise from transient dynamics, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
